findings.claim: The main theorem needlessly assumes `hf : Continuous f`, even though the file itself immediately notes this should be automatic for star-algebra equivalences of continuous endomorphism algebras. Requiring this extra hypothesis weakens the final API and forces downstream users to carry a proof that should be derivable internally.
findings.suggested_fix: Strengthen `StarAlgEquiv.eq_linearIsometryEquivConjStarAlgEquiv` to take only `f : (V →L[𝕜] V) ≃⋆ₐ[𝕜] (W →L[𝕜] W)` and prove continuity inside the theorem, then drop the extra `hf` argument from the `OrderIsoClass` instance as well.

findings.claim: This change removes the local `set_option linter.flexible false`, but the proof still relies on `simp_all` in a way that was explicitly marked as triggering the flexible linter. Unless you have rechecked that the linter now accepts this proof, this is a risky tidy-up in a non-style-only PR.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restore the local `set_option linter.flexible false in` around `isEquiv_iff_lt_one_iff`, or rewrite the proof to avoid the non-terminal `simp_all` calls altogether.

findings.claim: `BifibrantObject` is missing the analogue of `weakEquivalence_homMk_iff`, even though the file already provides that lemma for `CofibrantObject` and `FibrantObject`. This leaves the new API asymmetrical and makes it harder to use weak equivalences on morphisms in the bifibrant subcategory.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `@[simp] lemma weakEquivalence_homMk_iff [CategoryWithWeakEquivalences C] {X Y : C} [IsCofibrant X] [IsCofibrant Y] [IsFibrant X] [IsFibrant Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) : WeakEquivalence (homMk f) ↔ WeakEquivalence f := by simpa using weakEquivalence_iff_of_objectProperty (P := bifibrantObjects C) (f := ObjectProperty.homMk f)` (or the same two-line proof pattern used above).

findings.claim: The PR description says `injective_of_lt_imp_ne` should be renamed to `Function.Injective.of_lt_imp_ne` for dot notation, but the reviewed file still only defines the old top-level theorem. This leaves the API change incomplete and users still cannot write `f.Injective.of_lt_imp_ne ...`.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename/add this theorem as `Function.Injective.of_lt_imp_ne` (and, if desired for compatibility, keep `injective_of_lt_imp_ne` as a deprecated alias).

findings.claim: After introducing `Meromorphic` as the global shorthand, the file still leaves the two main global consequences (`countable_compl_analyticAt` at lines 614–617 and `measurable` at lines 622–631) only in the `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ` form. This makes the new predicate incomplete as a user-facing API: the natural theorems for the new notion are missing even though the stronger `Set.univ` versions already exist in the same file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add wrapper lemmas/theorems in the new API, e.g. `theorem countable_compl_analyticAt [SecondCountableTopology 𝕜] [CompleteSpace E] (h : Meromorphic f) : {z | AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z}ᶜ.Countable := (meromorphicOn_univ).2 h |> MeromorphicOn.countable_compl_analyticAt` and similarly `theorem measurable ... (h : Meromorphic f) : Measurable f := MeromorphicOn.measurable ((meromorphicOn_univ).2 h)` (or equivalent namespacing).
findings.evidence: Existing declarations `MeromorphicOn.countable_compl_analyticAt` (lines 614–617) and `MeromorphicOn.measurable` (lines 622–631) already prove the needed stronger facts for `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ`.

findings.claim: The stray `example` is leftover debugging code and should not be merged into the library. It introduces an unreferenced theorem-shaped artifact in the middle of the API with no documentation or downstream use.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the `example {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] ...` block entirely.

findings.claim: Most of these lemmas duplicate the generic `Finset` interval API already provided in `Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/SuccPred.lean`, specialized to `Fin`. In particular, the `add_one` lemmas are just the existing `succ` lemmas and the `sub_one` lemmas are just the existing `pred` lemmas, so adding a parallel `Fin`-specific family unnecessarily duplicates names and maintenance surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse or restate the existing generic lemmas instead of introducing new `Fin`-specific ones: e.g. `Iio_add_one_eq_Iic` ↔ `Finset.Iio_succ_eq_Iic`, `Iic_sub_one_eq_Iio` ↔ `Finset.Iic_pred_eq_Iio`, `Ici_add_one_eq_Ioi` ↔ `Finset.Ici_succ_eq_Ioi`, `Ioi_sub_one_eq_Ici` ↔ `Finset.Ioi_pred_eq_Ici`, `Icc_add_one_eq_Ioc` ↔ `Finset.Icc_succ_left_eq_Ioc`, `Ico_add_one_eq_Icc` ↔ `Finset.Ico_succ_right_eq_Icc`, `Ioo_add_one_eq_Ioc` ↔ `Finset.Ioo_succ_right_eq_Ioc`, `Ioc_sub_one_eq_Ioo` ↔ `Finset.Ioc_pred_right_eq_Ioo`, `Ioc_sub_one_eq_Icc` ↔ `Finset.Ioc_pred_left_eq_Icc`, `Ioo_sub_one_eq_Ico` ↔ `Finset.Ioo_pred_left_eq_Ioc`, and `Icc_sub_one_eq_Ico` ↔ `Finset.Icc_pred_right_eq_Ico`. If a `Fin` spelling is still desired, prove thin aliases directly from those generic declarations and use the established `succ`/`pred` naming.

findings.claim: The new names use `add_one`/`sub_one`, but the surrounding interval API is standardized on `succ`/`pred` (`Iio_succ_eq_Iic`, `Iic_pred_eq_Iio`, etc.). Introducing a second naming convention for the same endpoint perturbations makes the API harder to discover.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename any retained lemmas to the `succ`/`pred` convention, or better, rely on the existing generic `succ`/`pred` lemmas and add local rewriting lemmas only where `Fin.succ`/`Fin.pred` are genuinely unavailable.

findings.claim: `Dense.continuous_upperBounds` and `Dense.continuous_lowerBounds` duplicate existing closure/order API instead of reusing it. We already have `upperBounds_closure` and `lowerBounds_closure`, and even `isLUB_iff_of_subset_of_subset_closure` / `isGLB_iff_of_subset_of_subset_closure` in this same file; the new lemmas are just the special case `t = range f`, `s = f '' S`, with `range_subset_closure_image_dense` supplying the closure inclusion.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop these two new declarations, or replace them by short proofs of the later sup/inf lemmas via the existing closure API. Concretely, use `hf.range_subset_closure_image_dense hS` together with `upperBounds_closure` / `lowerBounds_closure` (or directly `isLUB_iff_of_subset_of_subset_closure` / `isGLB_iff_of_subset_of_subset_closure`) instead of adding new equalities of upper/lower bounds.
findings.evidence: Existing declarations: `upperBounds_closure` in `Mathlib/Topology/Order/OrderClosed.lean`, line 135; `lowerBounds_closure` there at line 384; `isLUB_iff_of_subset_of_subset_closure` / `isGLB_iff_of_subset_of_subset_closure` already in `Mathlib/Topology/Order/IsLUB.lean`, lines 148-157.

findings.claim: The `stacks 003B` tag has been moved from `Epi` onto `Mono`, which changes the API metadata rather than just deriving dual declarations. The Stacks tag should continue to annotate the original `Epi` declaration as before, with the dual tag copied to `Mono` via `to_dual` if desired.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore `@[stacks 003B]` on `class Epi`, and keep the dual generation on `Mono` without removing the original tag from `Epi` (for example, annotate `Epi` directly and use `to_dual` to populate the dual metadata as needed).

findings.claim: The file introduces new global constants and positivity facts as axioms (`cMoser`, `cGronwall`, `cSobolev`, etc.). In Mathlib, new mathematical content must be derived from existing theory or isolated behind explicit assumptions on the theorem, not added as unchecked axioms to the environment.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove these axioms. Either prove the needed estimates from existing analysis results, or parameterize the later lemmas/theorems by hypotheses supplying these constants and their properties locally.

findings.claim: The Fourier orthogonality/Fubini statements are added as axioms rather than proved from the existing `UnitAddCircle`/integration API. This makes the file extend the trusted kernel with unchecked analytic facts.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `fourier_ortho_integral` and `fubini_torus3` by actual lemmas proved from the existing Fourier and product-measure library, or keep the whole development in a non-Mathlib experiment file outside the library.

findings.claim: `fourierDecay` is defined as `True`, so `SmoothInitial` becomes vacuous: every initial datum is 'smooth'. This invalidates every later theorem that claims smoothness assumptions are being used materially.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `fourierDecay` the intended analytic content, or replace `SmoothInitial` by an existing non-vacuous smoothness predicate (for example a `ContDiff`-based formulation) and rework downstream statements accordingly.

findings.claim: The PDE content is trivialized: `spectralNSResidual` is identically `0`, and `GalerkinProjection` ignores both `N` and `t` and just returns the initial datum. As a result, `SolvesNavierStokes` and all 'Galerkin' regularity statements are about placeholder definitions rather than Navier–Stokes/Galerkin approximations.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the actual truncated dynamics and residual, with `GalerkinProjection` depending on the truncation and time evolution. If that is out of scope, theorems with names claiming Navier–Stokes or Galerkin results should not be added to Mathlib yet.

findings.claim: A second large block of unchecked axioms is introduced for the central analytical claims (`fourier_inversion`, `parseval_orthonormal`, `bkm_implies_regularity`, `vorticity_integrable`, Sobolev/Gronwall bounds, etc.). These are precisely the hard parts of the development, so the file is effectively postulating the main mathematics rather than formalizing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Eliminate these axioms by proving the lemmas from existing infrastructure, or move the statements to theorem assumptions in a section if you only want to study consequences conditionally.

findings.claim: The advertised main theorem does not use the temporal-lifting machinery or prove a Galerkin-limit existence result. `VorticityResponse.regularity` simply chooses `u := GalerkinProjection 1 u₀`, `p := 0`, obtains smoothness from the axiom `bkm_implies_regularity`, and satisfies the equation only because `spectralNSResidual` was defined to be `0`.
findings.suggested_fix: State a theorem that matches what is actually proved, or rework the development so the theorem is derived from genuine definitions and proved via the announced intermediate machinery.

findings.claim: The file ends with `#check`/`#print axioms` commands. These are debugging/development artifacts and are not kept in committed Mathlib source files.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the trailing `#check GalerkinLimit.smooth` and `#print axioms GalerkinLimit.smooth` commands before merge.

findings.claim: `set_option linter.style.commandStart false` is used to suppress style linting for the entire file. Since the file is new, it should normally be brought into conformance rather than disabling the linter globally.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the file-level linter suppression and adjust the command formatting to satisfy the style linter.

findings.claim: The docstring names a declaration `Pi.monoidal C`, but the declaration introduced here is the instance `Pi.monoidalCategory`. This leaves the public-facing API documentation inaccurate and makes it harder to discover the actual name via docs/search.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the docstring to mention the actual declaration name, e.g. `/-- `Pi.monoidalCategory` equips ... -/`, or make it a neutral instance docstring that does not name a nonexistent declaration.
findings.evidence: `target/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Pi/Monoidal.lean:81-83` shows the docstring mentions `Pi.monoidal C`, while the declaration on line 83 is `instance monoidalCategory : MonoidalCategory.{max w₁ v₁} (∀ i, C i)`.

findings.claim: This file introduces a parallel `Function.argmin`/`argminOn` API without proving the advertised connection to the existing `MinimalFor` API. That leaves duplication in the library: `Order/Minimal.lean` already has `exists_minimalFor_of_wellFoundedLT`, but the new file does not provide lemmas showing that `argmin`/`argminOn` are `MinimalFor` witnesses, which is the key interoperability this PR promises.
findings.suggested_fix: Add bridge lemmas such as `Function.minimalFor_argmin : MinimalFor (fun _ => True) f (argmin f)` and `Function.minimalFor_argminOn : MinimalFor (· ∈ s) f (argminOn f s hs)` (and finite variants as appropriate), and then derive the order-theoretic consequences from those. This reuses the existing `MinimalFor` vocabulary instead of leaving two disconnected APIs.

findings.claim: The docstring states the theorem is about `𝓢(ℝ, F)`, but the theorem itself is for arbitrary `𝓢(E, F)` under the section assumptions `[InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] ...`. This is misleading API documentation in a newly added theorem.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to match the actual statement, e.g. replace ``𝓢(ℝ, F)`` with ``𝓢(E, F)`` (or spell out the ambient assumptions if desired).

findings.claim: This adds `symm_prodComm` for `LinearEquiv.prodComm`, but the repository already has the identically named `[simp]` lemma for the linear-isometry version `LinearIsometry.prodComm`. Reusing the established naming pattern at two parallel API levels is fine, but here the new lemma appears to be a straightforward duplicate of an existing higher-level fact rather than filling a real API gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Please either drop this lemma if it is not needed by downstream code, or justify the addition by also using/proving the corresponding `LinearEquiv`-level API elsewhere. Evidence: `Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/LinearIsometry.lean` already contains `@[simp] theorem symm_prodComm [Module R E₂] : (prodComm R E E₂).symm = prodComm R E₂ E := rfl` at lines 1006–1008.

findings.claim: The new public theorem name `isSheafFor_ofArrows_iff_bijective_toCompabible` has a typo (`Compabible`), and it is already used by subsequent lemmas. Since this is exported API, the misspelling will leak to users and should be corrected before merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to `isSheafFor_ofArrows_iff_bijective_toCompatible` and update the downstream references in `isSheafFor_pullback_iff` and `isSheafFor_over_map_op_comp_ofArrows_iff`.
findings.evidence: target/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/IsSheafFor.lean:813 defines `isSheafFor_ofArrows_iff_bijective_toCompabible`, and the same misspelling is referenced again at lines 846 and 876.

findings.claim: The deprecated theorem `Ordinal.IsNormal.monotone` points users at `Order.IsNormal.strictMono`, but the replacement should be the newly added `Order.IsNormal.monotone`. Pointing to the stronger projection is inconsistent with the rest of the migration API and gives a worse deprecation hint than necessary.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the deprecation target on `Ordinal.IsNormal.monotone` from `Order.IsNormal.strictMono` to `Order.IsNormal.monotone`.

findings.claim: This rename introduces a new theorem name that is not exported: in the reviewed state, `orthogonalBilin_innerₗ` is not accessible after importing `Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Orthogonal`, while only the deprecated alias `bilinFormOfRealInner_orthogonal` remains visible. That is an API break for the intended replacement name.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `orthogonalBilin_innerₗ` exported at the top level (for example by adjusting the declaration so the theorem itself is the exported name, not only the deprecated alias), and verify with `#check orthogonalBilin_innerₗ` after importing `Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Orthogonal`.
findings.evidence: `lean_verify` on `import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Orthogonal; #check orthogonalBilin_innerₗ` reports `Unknown identifier 'orthogonalBilin_innerₗ'`, while `#check bilinFormOfRealInner_orthogonal` succeeds.

findings.claim: `mem_or_inv_mem_closure_baseOf` drops the `hv_inv` and `hf` hypotheses when rewriting with `Submonoid.closure_image_isMulIndecomposable_baseOf`, so the proof is relying on an underapplied theorem name instead of the actual lemma statement. Even if this happened to elaborate during local experimentation, it is not acceptable style/API for a library theorem because the required assumptions are hidden at the call site.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the first line as `rw [Submonoid.closure_image_isMulIndecomposable_baseOf v hv_inv f hf]` (and similarly keep explicit arguments for any other uses of this theorem), so the proof states clearly which hypotheses are being used.

findings.claim: The additive docstring for `IsMulIndecomposable.baseOf` has a typo: 'crystallogrphic' should be 'crystallographic'.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the typo in the `@[to_additive]` docstring.

findings.claim: The new PR leaves an existing typo in the surrounding API docs: the instance docstring says `Multipilication` instead of `Multiplication`. Since this PR is already touching the nearby lines, we should clean that up here.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to `/-- Multiplication in `R` transfers to Addition in `ArchimedeanClass R`. -/`.

findings.claim: The new subtraction API is only half-complete: you add `sub_right_injective_of_ne_top` / `sub_right_inj_of_ne_top`, but there is no matching right-side monotonicity/cancellation family (`sub_right_strictMono_of_ne_top`, `sub_lt_sub_iff_right_of_ne_top`, `sub_le_sub_iff_right_of_ne_top`). This leaves the PR's stated goal of adding monotonicity lemmas for subtraction asymmetric and makes the new injectivity lemma harder to use.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the right-hand subtraction counterparts, e.g. `lemma sub_right_strictMono_of_ne_top (a) (h : a ≠ ⊤) : StrictAnti fun x ↦ a - x` (or the appropriately named monotonicity/antitonicity statement), together with the corresponding `[simp]` iff lemmas for `<` and `≤`, or else drop `sub_right_injective_of_ne_top` from this PR if you do not want to expose that side of the API yet.

findings.claim: The theorem docstrings in this block are now inaccurate: `norm_deriv_le_div_of_mapsTo_ball` still says the image is an open ball, and the next two still describe the old self-map hypotheses (`f c = c`, codomain `ℂ`, conclusion about `dist (f z) c`). This leaves the API documentation inconsistent with the actual statements after the weakening/generalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the docstrings to match the new declarations: say `closedBall (f c) R₂` for `norm_deriv_le_div_of_mapsTo_ball`; for `norm_deriv_le_one_of_mapsTo_ball`, describe mapping `ball c R` into `closedBall (f c) R` (no separate `hc` hypothesis); and for `dist_le_dist_of_mapsTo_ball_self`, describe the actual conclusion `dist (f z) (f c) ≤ dist z c` and, if desired, mention the codomain-generalized version separately.
findings.evidence: `target/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Schwarz.lean` lines 137-163: the theorem statements use `closedBall (f c) ...`, while lines 135, 153, and 160 in the attached docstrings still describe the old open-ball/self-map assumptions.

findings.claim: The two new lemmas are missing docstrings, which makes this section inconsistent with the adjacent `iteratedDeriv_comp_const_add` / `iteratedDeriv_comp_add_const` API and leaves the generated docs incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `/-- ... -/` comments for `iteratedDeriv_comp_sub_const` and `iteratedDeriv_comp_const_sub`, mirroring the existing translation-lemma documentation style.

findings.claim: `IntrinsicStar.starLinearEquiv_eq` is too generically named for a theorem about the intrinsic star on linear maps, and it conflicts with the existing naming pattern where analogous transport lemmas are specialized (for example `starLinearEquiv_tensor`). As written, this name is likely to be ambiguous in imports and hard to discover.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename this lemma to a linear-map-specific name such as `starLinearEquiv_linearMap` (or `IntrinsicStar.starLinearEquiv_linearMap`) so it matches the existing API style. Evidence: `Mathlib/Algebra/Star/TensorProduct.lean` already uses the specialized name `starLinearEquiv_tensor` for the analogous statement `starLinearEquiv R (A := A ⊗[R] B) = congr (starLinearEquiv R) (starLinearEquiv R)`.

findings.claim: The new lemma name is backwards relative to the surrounding `card_*` API and hides the subject of the statement. In this file, cardinality lemmas are consistently named starting with `card_...`, so `eq_card_diff_of_sdiff` is hard to discover next to `card_sdiff`, `card_sdiff_of_subset`, and `le_card_sdiff`.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename this to a `card_*` name matching the existing API, e.g. `card_sub_card_eq_card_sdiff_sub_card_sdiff` (or another `card_...` variant agreed on by maintainers), and keep the current statement.
findings.evidence: The surrounding declarations in `Mathlib/Data/Finset/Card.lean` are `card_sdiff_of_subset`, `card_sdiff`, `card_sdiff_add_card_eq_card`, `le_card_sdiff`, `card_sdiff_add_card_inter`, `card_sdiff_le_card_sdiff_iff`, `card_sdiff_lt_card_sdiff_iff`, and `card_sdiff_eq_card_sdiff_iff`.
